body_markdown:
This year, Broad Arrow moved its Monterey auction from the Monterey Jet Center to the more spacious Quail Golf Club in nearby Carmel, becoming the official auction partner of the glitzy “The Quail by The Peninsula, A Motorsports Gathering” in the process. This was a spot held for many years prior by Bonhams, which moved to Laguna Seca Raceway for its 2026 auction.


Broad Arrow has only been hosting a Monterey auction since 2022, and this year brought the most vehicles as well as the highest sales totals. As elsewhere throughout Monterey Car Week 2026, modern supercars won the day at the Quail, with multiple Bugattis, Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and rare-spec Porsches garnering the most attention


We were on the ground in Monterey and looked over the most important cars crossing the block over the course of the week. Here, we examine some of the favorites from Broad Arrow.


## Lot 148: 1994 Toyota TRD 3000GT


Broad Arrow


**Sold for $582,500**


*Chassis no. JT2JA82J5R0011586. White over black leather. Original, #2 condition.*


**Equipment:** 3.0L twin-turbo straight-six, six-speed, body kit, Graphic Control Computer ECU, Recaro seats, carbon fiber interior trim, Defi gauges.


**Condition:** One of 35 Supra 3000GTs produced by Toyota TRD and the only example converted from a U.S. market car. Reportedly bought new in California by a Japanese tourist, shipped back to Japan in early 1994, and converted by TRD in 2001. Imported to the U.S. this summer after long-term Danish ownership. The original paint and bodywork remain excellent with no noticeable damage. The engine compartment shows little indication of serious use or or finish degradation. The interior shows some minor wear to the seats, otherwise it remains in very good condition. An exceptionally rare Supra in superb condition.


Broad Arrow


Broad Arrow


Broad Arrow


**Bottom line:** Essentially a racier[Supra](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/toyota/supra/1993/1993-toyota-supra-mk_iv_turbo?id=aCn1I000000kAwdSAE) inspired by Toyota’s Japanese Grand Touring Championship (JGTC) cars, the TRD 3000GT is so rare that it’s an obscure thing even to JDM nerds. But that rarity, in addition to the ideal specs, pushed it to a huge price. This is the most expensive Supra ever sold at auction, eclipsing the *Fast and Furious* hero car that sold for[$550k](https://www.barrett-jackson.com/las-vegas-2021/docket/vehicle/1994-toyota-supra-fast-furious-movie-car-247854) in 2021.


## Lot 168: 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo


Broad Arrow


**Sold for** **$500,000**


*Chassis no. WP0ZZZ99ZTS371675. Violet Blue Metallic over Florence Grey leather. Visually maintained, largely original, #2- condition.*


**Equipment:** 3601cc/400hp, six-speed, body-color Turbo Twist wheels, red calipers, sunroof, wood dash and interior trim, white gauges.


**Condition:** Paint to Sample and Leather to Sample. Light Rootwood package for the interior. Recommissioned by RUF in 2023. Showing 32,245 km (20,036 miles). Numerous chips on the nose and light age to the brakes. Lightly wrinkled leather. Highly optioned and striking, with a few flaws.


Broad Arrow


**Bottom line:** Options and colors matter in the collector car world, and Porsche people pore over these details more than anybody. “Paint to Sample” (PTS) are magic words and take this car from a very good 993 Turbo to an exceptional[993 Turbo](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/porsche/911/1996/1996-porsche-911-turbo?id=aCn1I000000DOBGSA4) . It’s a condition #2- car that sold for slightly over condition #1 money.


## Lot 174: 1996 Nissan NISMO 400R


Broad Arrow


**Sold for $857,500**


*Chassis no. BCNR33023463* . *Sonic Silver with black graphics over black cloth. Original, #2- condition.*


**Equipment:** 2771cc/400hp twin-turbo straight-six, titanium exhaust, five-speed, white Rays three-piece wheels, Bridgestone Potenza tires, power windows, auxiliary gauges added, HKS turbo timer.


**Condition:** Number 20 of 44 NISMO 400Rs produced, imported after nearly 30 years of continuous ownership in Japan. Fantastic, original paint with only a pair of minor chips on the hood. The NISMO lettering on the intercooler is faded, and the exposed carbon fiber on the rear spoiler has some finish fade. The engine bay presents very well and shows minor use, and the underbody is extremely clean. The interior is clean and the seats do not exhibit wear. A gorgeous, rare-spec Skyline that appears barely driven, even though its odometer reads 93,033 km (57,808 miles).


**Bottom line:** A JDM darling, the[400R](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/nissan/skyline/1996/1996-nissan-skyline-gt~r_nismo_400r?id=aCn1I000000kJZJSA2) is on many a “must have” list, but there are only a few dozen out there and few of those have reached the U.S. They have the makings of a million-dollar modern collectible but haven’t quite gotten there yet. Recent auction results (there are just three of them) have included $995K, $918K, and this $857,500 result.


## Lot 186: 1991 Venturi 111 Cup


Broad Arrow


**Sold for** **$53,200**


*Chassis no. VK8CUP11191CH0019. Black over tan leather. Original, #2- condition.*


**Equipment:** 2.0L turbo four-cylinder, five-speed, alloy wheels, Michelin tires, wood dash and shift knob, power windows, air conditioning.


**Condition:** Showing 1843 km (1145 miles). Very good paint. Slightly stretched upholstery. The Venturi badge and the engine cover vents are showing some age. A neat example of the entry-level model from this little-known French marque.


**Bottom line:** Virtually unknown in this country, French automaker Venturi had a real go of it in the 1980s and ’90s, building exotic cars for the road and track to compete with the likes of Porsche and Ferrari, with the majority of its cars powered by the unlikeliest of mills—the PRV (Peugeot-Renault-Volvo) V-6—albeit in modified and turbocharged form. A Venturi is an unusual sight anywhere, but this car is even more unusual. Given the Italian market’s rather punitive tax laws on automobiles over 2.0 liters, Venturi built the 111 Cup specifically for that country, with all the looks of its faster models but with a smaller turbocharged Renault four-cylinder behind the driver.


The market for Venturis in the United States is virtually nonexistent, but Broad Arrow sold this car in Amelia Island three years ago for $56,000. It had 350 km on it at the time. Driving it only about 1000 miles and selling it for thousands less a few years later isn’t the most sensible way to enjoy an unusual sports car, but people have certainly lost a lot more money in this hobby.


## Lot 165: 1957 Aston Martin DB2/4 Mk III Coupe


Broad Arrow


**Sold for $201,600**


*Chassis no. AM30031380. Light metallic blue over blue leather. Older restoration, #2- condition.*


**Equipment:** LHD. 2922cc/140hp straight-six, BorgWarner five-speed, wire wheels, Vredestein tires, woodrim steering wheel, Smiths gauges and dash clock, Quicksilver exhaust, Blaupunkt speakers.


**Condition:** One of 462 coupes built. Good chrome. A few small chips and cracks on the hood. Large crack at the bottom of the right A-pillar. Small cracks in the taillight lenses. Imperfect panel fit. Some weather stripping has come off on the driver’s side. Nice interior. Reasonably well-restored and mildly upgraded.


**Bottom line:** An evolution of the DB2/4 Mark II, the[Mark III](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/aston_martin/db/1957/1957-aston_martin-db-mk_iii?id=aCn1I000000CrMHSA0) was mechanically similar to its predecessor, but its bodywork was far prettier. It also previewed the curves of the DB4, DB5, and DB6, as well as the shape of the grille that has been an Aston Martin signature since.


This one sold for $275,000 on Bring a Trailer in 2022, but was a no-sale on the platform last year at a $200K high bid. Then it went to PCARMARKET a month later but had even less luck at a $105K high bid. The softer market recently for vintage Astons was reflected in Broad Arrow’s $210,000–$230,000 estimate, and the seller wisely took a fair offer, since a higher one isn’t likely to come elsewhere any time soon.


## Lot 177: 1987 Porsche 928 Clubsport Prototype


Broad Arrow


**Sold for** **$162,400**


*Chassis no. WP0ZZZ92ZHS841983. Grand Prix White over black leather. Unrestored original, #3+ condition.*


**Equipment:** 5.0L/330hp V-8, dog-leg five-speed, alloy wheels, rear spoiler, power windows, air conditioning, Blaupunkt cassette.


**Condition:** Delivered new to race driver Jochen Mass, who used it to drive to Group C races in period. The first of four lightweight Clubsport pre-production prototypes built. Known ownership history from new. Showing 109,321 km (67,929 miles) and unrestored, with a few chips in the nose and a ding in the right rear wheel. Some dirt and oxidation underneath. Lightly worn interior. An unremarkable driver condition-wise, but in terms of equipment and history it’s very cool.


**Bottom line:** Porsche provided four of these Clubsport prototypes to works drivers Jochen Mass, Derek Bell, Hans-Joachim Stuck, and Bob Wollek, and Mass reportedly put the majority of the mileage on this one’s odometer. The history is very interesting and the car is, too, so Broad Arrow’s $250K–$350K estimate seemed perfectly realistic. The[928](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/search?q=porsche+928) just isn’t a market darling, however, and perhaps this one got a bit lost in the sea of rare-spec 911s, RUFs, and Singers on offer at the Quail auction.


## Lot 238: 1968 Lamborghini Miura P400 S


Broad Arrow


**Sold for** **$4,075,000**


*Chassis no. 3832; Engine no. 2619* . *Azzurro Mexico Metallizzato over Nero leather with blue cloth inserts. Older restoration, #2- condition.*


**Equipment:** 3929cc/370hp V-12, five-speed, Campagnolo wheels, leather-wrapped steering wheel, power windows.


**Condition:** The 13th of 338 Miura Ss built. Showing 7838 km (4870 miles) that are represented as actual. Matching numbers. Two tiny chips in the nose. Small scratches at the front edge of the driver’s door. Beautiful interior. An older restoration.


Broad Arrow


Broad Arrow


**Bottom line:** Gooding Christie’s sold this car last year, painted in red and with 18 fewer kilometers on the clock, for $2.45M. There is no mention of the color change in Broad Arrow’s catalog, but the swing in price is due less to any difference in the car’s presentation and more to the rise in[Miura](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/search?q=lamborghini+miura) values over the past 12 months, along with the general exuberance mid-engine exotics—even older ones—brought in Monterey this year. The car’s high estimate was $3.6M.


## Lot 269: 2011 Bugatti Veyron 16.4 Grand Sport


Broad Arrow


**Sold for** **$3,305,000**


*Chassis no. VF9SK2C2XBM795030. White over saddle leather. Original, #2- condition.*


**Equipment:** 7993cc/1001hp quad-turbo W-16, automatic.


**Condition:** Represented with 8595 miles and as one of 150 built. Slightly flattened seat bottoms and some marks around the contact points for the roof. Otherwise it looks lovely. Let’s just hope it doesn’t need a service or a set of tires any time soon.


**Bottom line:** With its 253-mph top speed and seven-figure price tag, the[Veyron](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/search?q=bugatti+veyron) was the high-performance benchmark of the 2000s, and its success arguably helped the growth of the boutique hypercar market that has taken place in the 20 years since the resurgent Bugatti’s debut. They’ll therefore always be collectible, and they’ve gotten more expensive over the last three or four years, but prices have really shot up in 2026. They apparently still have room to grow, because this nice but not exceptional example sold for a record for the model, beating the previous record by only 3.6% which was set 18 years ago by chassis 001 at Gooding Pebble Beach 2008.


## Lot 155: 1954 Maserati A6GCS by Fiandri & Malagoli


Broad Arrow


**Sold for** **$2,012,500**


*Chassis no. 2078. Red over black leather. Older restoration, #2- condition.*


**Equipment:** 2.0L straight-six, four-speed, painted Borrani wire wheels, woodrim steering wheel, blue Jaeger gauges.


**Condition:** Raced in period by works driver Luigi Musso. Won its class at the Giro delle Calabrie, Circuito di Seniia, and RAC Tourist Trophy. National class champion in hill climb competition in Italy. Subsequent race history in Argentina. Later restored and used in multiple Mille Miglia Storicas as well as other vintage racing events. In current ownership for almost 30 years. Powered by a reproduction engine, though an original one is included in the sale, along with another reproduction. Good older paint. Some scuffs in the wheels. Slightly dry and wrinkled seats. A lovely little car.


**Bottom line:** A very cool and eminently usable historic racer that is eligible for top-level historic events all over the world, it has also been extensively researched by Maserati authority Dr. Adolfo Orsi, Jr. This was a star lot of the Broad Arrow auction, even if it wasn’t the most expensive result.


## Lot 183: 1981 Porsche 924 Carrera GTR


Broad Arrow


**Sold for** **$375,000**


*Chassis no. WP0ZZZ93ZBS720011. Silver, black, and blue over black. Older restoration, #3+ condition.*


**Equipment:** 2.0L/375hp turbo four-cylinder, five-speed.


**Condition:** 1982 24 Hours of Le Mans IMSA GTO class winner. One of 17 Porsche 924 Carrera GTRs. Campaigned by Brumos three times at the Daytona 24 Hours and Sebring 12 Hours. Later restored and shown at the 2012 Amelia Island Concours. Offered with a valid FIA HTP and eligible for both European and U.S. historic racing. The paint presents well, even with stone chips on the quarter panels. The engine shows some aging but not excessively so, and the interior is aged with finish wear to the steering wheel, faded dash, and faded safety harnesses. An important racing Porsche. Arguably the quickest and the coolest 924 of them all.


**Bottom line:** Despite the[924’s](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/porsche/924/1981/1981-porsche-924-base?id=aCn1I000000DLMWSA4) humble beginnings as an Audi-engined entry-level model, Porsche put serious effort into developing it and racing it, creating the 924 Turbo, 924 Carrera GT, 924 Carrera GTS, and Carrera GTR. Given their rarity and pedigree, the latter three models exist in a completely different universe in terms of collectibility compared to the standard models, some of which can still be bought for four-figure prices. Several Carrera GTSs and GTRs have sold for more than $400K in recent years, so given this one’s endurance racing history, Broad Arrow’s $600K low estimate didn’t seem crazy, but in the end the seller cut it loose for far less.


## Lot 266: 2014 Aston Martin Vanquish Centenary Edition


Broad Arrow


**Sold for** **$417,500**


*Chassis no. SCFLDCFPXEGJ01702. Midnight Blue Metallic and black over black and blue leather. Original, #2 condition.*


**Equipment:** 5999cc/565hp V-12, paddle shifters, Pirelli P Zero tires.


**Condition:** Ex-Daniel Craig, the seventh (car 007, get it?) of 100 built. Just 1162 miles and no real signs of use.


**Bottom line:** Had this car been ordered by a non-movie star, it would have cost around $300K when new. Broad Arrow reasoned that the car had depreciated like, well, a late-model Aston Martin, and estimated $175K–$225K for it. Celebrity cachet does not always add value to a collector car, and when it does, the “how much” is hard to quantify. In this case, two motivated buyers happened to spy an Aston owned by a James Bond–playing actor, and they had to have it.


## Lot 277: 2003 Ferrari Enzo


Broad Arrow


**Sold for** **$10,675,000**


*Chassis no. ZFFCW56A130132652. Nero DS over Rosso leather. Original, #2 condition.*


**Equipment:** 5999cc/660hp V-12, black calipers, Bridgestone Potenza Scuderia tires.


**Condition:** Represented as one of 12 U.S.-spec Enzos finished in Nero, and only three of those have this Rosso interior. Ferrari Classiche certified and recent $80,000 service and detail work. Exceptional paint and body. The engine is perfectly detailed, and the interior shows little usage. Showing 13,268 miles but looks like a car with even fewer. A beautifully kept Enzo.


**Bottom line:** Ten months ago, a $10.7M[Enzo](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/ferrari/enzo/2003/2003-ferrari-enzo-base?id=aCn1I000000DI6oSAG) would have been a shocking, record-smashing amount. But in August of 2026, it almost seems normal, and this wasn’t even the most expensive Enzo in Monterey this year, as Mecum sold a 595-mile example for[$12.1M](https://www.mecum.com/lots/1176628/2003-ferrari-enzo/) . Other Enzos sold at auction this year have ranged from €6,530,000 ($7.6M) to $17.9M, with mileage and color being the big determining factors.


The post[12 Important Cars from the 2026 Broad Arrow Quail Auction](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/12-important-cars-from-the-2026-broad-arrow-quail-auction/) appeared first on[Hagerty Media](https://www.hagerty.com/media) .
